prompt: In North Carolina, a driver 21 or older can be convicted of driving while impaired (DWI) based on a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of at least what level?
choices: 0.10 percent
0.02 percent
0.08 percent
0.05 percent
explanation: DWI can be proven by a BAC of 0.08 percent or more (0.04 in a commercial motor vehicle), or by showing your physical or mental faculties are appreciably impaired.

prompt: What BAC is enough for a DWI when you are driving a commercial motor vehicle in North Carolina?
choices: 0.02 or more
0.06 or more
0.08 or more
0.04 or more
explanation: For commercial motor vehicle drivers the limit is 0.04, half the 0.08 limit that applies in a regular car.

prompt: A 19-year-old is convicted of driving with alcohol in their body, even though their BAC was only 0.03. What happens to their North Carolina license?
choices: They get 3 points but keep the license
It is revoked for one year
Nothing, because the BAC was under 0.08
It is suspended for 30 days
explanation: For drivers under 21, any amount of alcohol or drugs in the body is an offense. A conviction brings a one-year license revocation.

prompt: After being charged with DWI, a driver refuses to take the required breath test. What license penalty follows?
choices: An immediate revocation of at least 30 days plus a minimum 12-month DMV revocation
A 30-day revocation only
A warning, because the test is voluntary
A 6-month suspension that can be avoided by paying a fine
explanation: Refusing a required chemical test brings an immediate revocation of at least 30 days and an additional minimum 12-month revocation by DMV. The refusal can also be used as evidence in court.

prompt: What license penalty does North Carolina require for a first DWI conviction?
choices: Mandatory revocation for one year
Mandatory revocation for 90 days
Suspension for 30 days
Four years of revocation
explanation: A first DWI conviction brings a mandatory one-year license revocation. Four years applies to a second conviction when the prior offense was within three years.

prompt: A 17-year-old provisional licensee drinks one beer and later drives. If convicted, what is the penalty?
choices: A one-year license revocation
No penalty if the BAC was under 0.02
A 30-day suspension
A fine only, with no effect on the license
explanation: It is unlawful for a provisional licensee (under 18) to drive after consuming any amount of alcohol or drugs. A conviction brings a one-year revocation.

prompt: In the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle on a North Carolina highway, which alcoholic beverages are prohibited?
choices: Only liquor, not beer or wine
None, if the driver is not drinking
Open or closed containers
Only open containers
explanation: NC DWI laws prohibit possessing alcoholic beverages, open or closed, in the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle on any highway, street or public vehicular area.

prompt: Which of these do North Carolina's DWI laws specifically prohibit for the driver of a car?
choices: Transporting an open container of an alcoholic beverage, including in the passenger area
Carrying a sealed container of alcohol in the trunk
Driving home from a store after buying alcohol
Giving a ride to a passenger who has been drinking
explanation: NC DWI laws prohibit drinking any alcoholic beverage, including beer, while driving and transporting an open container of alcohol, including in the passenger area of the car.

prompt: At what age may an eligible driver with a provisional license upgrade to a regular Class C driver license?
explanation: Drivers under 18 are provisional licensees. At age 18, eligible drivers may upgrade to a regular Class C license online.

prompt: What is the youngest age at which a North Carolina teen can get a Level 1 Limited Learner Permit?
explanation: A teen at least 15 years old who has completed an approved driver education course may apply for a Level 1 Limited Learner Permit.

prompt: Before a teen under 18 can test for a learner permit, what driver education must they have completed?
choices: At least 30 hours of classroom and 6 hours of behind-the-wheel instruction
At least 20 hours of classroom and 10 hours behind the wheel
An online course of any length
A 4-hour drug and alcohol class only
explanation: Applicants under 18 must show a certificate for an approved driver education course of at least 30 hours classroom and 6 hours behind-the-wheel instruction.

prompt: During the first six months of a Level 1 Limited Learner Permit, when may the permit holder drive?
choices: Daylight hours only, with any licensed adult
Between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m., with the supervising driver
Any time, with the supervising driver
Between 6 a.m. and 10 p.m., alone
explanation: For the first six months, a Level 1 permit allows driving from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. with the supervising driver. After six months, the holder may drive at any time with a supervising driver.

prompt: How long must a teen hold the Level 1 Limited Learner Permit before applying for a Level 2 Limited Provisional License?
choices: Three months
Nine months
Six months
Twelve months
explanation: The Level 1 permit must be held for nine months before applying for a Limited Provisional License.

prompt: How much supervised driving must the Level 1 driving log show, and how much of it must be at night?
choices: 60 hours total, with at least 10 at night
50 hours total, with at least 10 at night
60 hours total, with at least 15 at night
40 hours total, with at least 6 at night
explanation: The driving log must show at least 60 hours of driving, with at least 10 hours at night. It is signed by the supervising driver and turned in when applying for the Level 2 license.

prompt: Which person may serve as the supervising driver for a teen with a Level 1 permit?
choices: An 18-year-old sibling with a valid license
Any adult who has held a license for one year
A friend's parent with a learner permit
A grandparent who has held a valid license for at least five years
explanation: A supervising driver must be a parent, grandparent, guardian, or responsible person approved by the parent or guardian. They must hold a valid license and have been licensed for at least five years.

prompt: What is the minimum age for a Level 2 Limited Provisional License in North Carolina?
explanation: Level 2 drivers must be at least 16 but under 18, and must have held the Level 1 permit for nine months.

prompt: A 16-year-old with a Level 2 Limited Provisional License wants to drive alone to a friend's house at 10 p.m. Is this allowed?
choices: No, Level 2 drivers may never drive after dark
No, a supervising driver is needed after 9 p.m. unless driving directly to or from work or volunteer emergency service
Yes, Level 2 has no time limits
Yes, if a parent gives permission by phone
explanation: Level 2 drivers may drive unsupervised only from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m., or at any time directly to or from work or volunteer fire, rescue or EMS duty if they are a member.

prompt: A Level 2 driver is driving unsupervised to the mall on a Saturday. Two 16-year-old friends who do not live with the driver want a ride. What does the law allow?
choices: Only one of the friends may ride
The two friends may ride if they wear seat belts
The two friends may ride because they are under 18, not under 21
No passengers at all are allowed
explanation: Unsupervised Level 2 drivers may carry only one passenger under 21 who is not a household member. A second non-household passenger under 21 is allowed only when that passenger is a student riding directly to or from school.

prompt: How long must a driver hold a Level 2 Limited Provisional License before applying for a Level 3 Full Provisional License?
choices: At least six months
At least nine months
At least twelve months
At least three months
explanation: A Level 2 license must be held at least six months before applying for the Full Provisional License.

prompt: A teen wants to move up from Level 1 to Level 2. Which recent conviction would stop them from graduating?
choices: A parking ticket within the past six months
Any conviction within the past three years
A school tardy record
A seat belt infraction within the past six months
explanation: Before moving up a level, the teen must have no convictions of moving violations, seat belt infractions or cell phone infractions in the preceding six months.

prompt: Which restriction still applies to a 17-year-old with a Level 3 Full Provisional License?
choices: No cell phone use while driving, except certain emergency calls
Driving only between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m.
Only one non-family passenger under 21
A supervising driver must ride along
explanation: Level 3 removes the time, supervision and passenger limits, but drivers under 18 may still not use a cell phone while driving, except for emergency calls to listed contacts.

prompt: Under North Carolina's 'Lose Control/Lose Your License' rule, what causes a student to lose their license?
choices: Any detention or school discipline
A school suspension of more than 10 consecutive days
Two unexcused absences in a row
A failing grade in driver education
explanation: A student loses their license if suspended for more than 10 consecutive days, or assigned to an alternative educational setting for discipline for more than 10 consecutive days. The loss lasts 12 months.

prompt: At how many points may a North Carolina driver be assigned to a driver improvement clinic?
choices: 7 points
5 points
10 points
12 points
explanation: With seven points, you may be assigned to a driver improvement clinic. Completing it removes three points from your record.

prompt: How many license points within a three-year period can lead to suspension of a North Carolina license?
choices: 8 points
10 points
15 points
12 points
explanation: Reaching 12 points within three years can lead to suspension. After reinstatement, just 8 points within three years can bring a second suspension.

prompt: How many license points does a conviction for passing a stopped school bus carry for a regular (non-commercial) driver?
explanation: Passing a stopped school bus is one of the highest point values for a regular driver: 5 points (8 in a commercial vehicle). Aggressive driving is also 5.

prompt: A driver is convicted of going 72 mph in a 55 mph zone. What happens to their driving privilege?
choices: Nothing beyond a fine, since it is a first offense
It is revoked for one year
It is suspended only if they also had a crash
It is revoked for at least 30 days
explanation: Driving more than 15 mph over the limit at a speed above 55 mph brings a revocation of at least 30 days. 72 mph in a 55 zone is 17 mph over.

prompt: A 17-year-old provisional licensee is convicted of a second moving violation within 12 months. What can happen?
choices: A one-year revocation
Nothing until a fourth violation
A 30-day license suspension
A 6-month suspension
explanation: Provisional licensees may be suspended for 30 days for a second moving violation in 12 months, 90 days for a third and six months for a fourth.

prompt: What are North Carolina's minimum liability insurance amounts for a private passenger vehicle?
choices: $50,000 per person, $100,000 per crash, $25,000 property damage
$30,000 per person injured, $60,000 per crash for injuries, $25,000 property damage
$25,000 per person, $50,000 per crash, $25,000 property damage
$30,000 per person, $60,000 per crash, $15,000 property damage
explanation: NC requires at least $30,000 for injury to one person, $60,000 for all injuries in a crash, and $25,000 for property damage.

prompt: Your car insurance lapses, but your car still has a valid NC license plate. What can happen?
choices: Nothing, if you renew within the insurer's 30-day grace period
Only your driver license is affected
Your registration is canceled for one year
The plate can be revoked for 30 days and you may face a penalty, because NC has no grace period
explanation: Owners must keep continuous liability insurance while the plate is valid. A lapse can lead to plate revocation for 30 days and a fine or penalty. NC does not honor an insurer's grace period; surrender the plate before canceling coverage.

prompt: You just moved to North Carolina. How long do you have to get a North Carolina driver license?
choices: 60 days after establishing residence
30 days after establishing residence
90 days after establishing residence
One year after establishing residence
explanation: New residents have 60 days after establishing residence to get an NC license or learner permit. Holders of an out-of-state CDL have only 30 days to get an NC CDL.

prompt: Which statement about texting applies to every North Carolina driver, regardless of age?
choices: Texting is only illegal for drivers under 18
Reading texts is legal as long as you do not type
It is unlawful to use a cell phone for email or text messages while operating a vehicle on a public street or highway
Texting is legal on streets with a speed limit under 35 mph
explanation: NC law makes it unlawful for any driver to use a cell phone for email or text messages while operating a vehicle on a public street, highway or public vehicular area.

prompt: A 17-year-old with a Level 3 Full Provisional License wants to make a hands-free call to a friend while driving. Is this legal?
choices: Yes, hands-free calls are allowed at Level 3
Yes, if the phone is mounted on the dashboard
Only on roads with a speed limit under 45 mph
No, drivers under 18 may not use a cell phone or related technology while driving
explanation: Drivers under 18 may not use a cell phone or any technology associated with one while driving, including hands-free. The exceptions are emergency calls.

prompt: A 16-year-old with a Level 2 license has an emergency while driving. Which call does the law allow?
choices: A call to their parent, legal guardian or spouse about the emergency
A call to a friend to say they are running late
A call to a coworker to swap shifts
No calls of any kind
explanation: Under 18, cell phone use while driving is banned, except emergency calls to an emergency operator, hospital or doctor, ambulance service, fire department, law enforcement, or a parent, legal guardian or spouse.

prompt: Which North Carolina drivers may not use a cell phone at all while driving, no matter their age?
choices: Taxi drivers
Delivery drivers
Motorcycle riders
School bus drivers
explanation: No one may operate a school bus on a public street, highway or public vehicular area while using a cell phone or other mobile device technology.

prompt: Who must wear a seat belt in a North Carolina vehicle that was manufactured with seat belts?
choices: Only passengers under 18
Only people in vehicles without air bags
The driver and all passengers, front and back
Only the driver and front-seat passenger
explanation: The driver and all passengers must have a seat belt fastened whenever the vehicle is moving forward on a street or highway, even if the vehicle has air bags.

prompt: A 6-year-old who weighs 55 pounds is riding in your car. What does North Carolina law require?
choices: The child must be in a weight-appropriate child restraint
An adult seat belt alone is enough
The child may ride unbuckled in the back seat
The child may ride in the front seat with an adult seat belt
explanation: A child under age 8 who weighs less than 80 pounds must be secured in a weight-appropriate child passenger restraint system.

prompt: Your car has an active passenger-side front air bag and a back seat. Where must a 3-year-old who weighs 30 pounds ride?
choices: In the rear seat, unless the child seat is designed for use with a front air bag
In the front seat so the driver can watch the child
Anywhere, as long as the child is in a car seat
In the front seat only if the seat is moved all the way back
explanation: With an active front air bag and a rear seat available, a child under 5 and weighing less than 40 pounds must be secured in the rear seat, unless the restraint is designed for use with a front air bag.

prompt: North Carolina's child passenger law requires the driver to make sure which passengers are properly restrained?
choices: Every passenger younger than 16
Only children under 8
Only children under 5
Only children in the front seat
explanation: Every driver carrying passengers under 16 must make sure each of them is secured in a child restraint or seat belt that meets federal standards.

prompt: Can a 12-year-old ride in the open bed of a pickup truck on a North Carolina highway?
choices: Yes, if the tailgate is closed
Yes, on roads with speed limits under 35 mph
Yes, if a parent is driving
Not unless an exemption applies, such as an adult in the bed supervising the child
explanation: NC law prohibits children under 16 from riding in an open pickup bed. Exemptions include an adult in the bed supervising, an approved seat belt, an emergency, a parade or agricultural work.

prompt: Unless another limit is posted, what is the speed limit in North Carolina cities and towns?
choices: 45 mph
35 mph
25 mph
30 mph
explanation: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit is 35 mph in cities and towns.

prompt: Unless another limit is posted, what is the maximum speed outside cities and towns in North Carolina?
choices: 65 mph
55 mph
45 mph
60 mph
explanation: The handbook's maximum speed limit outside cities and towns is 55 mph. Higher limits apply only where posted, such as up to 70 mph on interstates.

prompt: What is the highest speed limit that may be posted on North Carolina interstates?
choices: 75 mph
80 mph
70 mph
65 mph
explanation: The handbook lists 70 mph as the maximum speed limit for interstates.

prompt: What is the maximum speed limit for a school bus in North Carolina?
choices: 40 mph
45 mph
35 mph
55 mph
explanation: School buses are limited to 45 mph. School activity buses may go up to 55 mph.

prompt: What following distance rule does the North Carolina handbook teach?
choices: The six-second rule
The two-second rule
The one-car-length-per-10-mph rule
The four-second rule
explanation: Allow two seconds between the moment the vehicle ahead passes a point and the moment you reach it. Increase it in bad conditions.

prompt: According to the North Carolina handbook, where does a highway work zone begin and end?
choices: Within 500 feet of any construction equipment
Only between orange barrels
From the first sign that marks the start of the work zone to the last sign that marks its end
Only where workers are present
explanation: A highway work zone is the area between the first sign marking its beginning and the last sign marking its end. An extra speeding penalty applies if a sign listing it is posted at the start.

prompt: On a multi-lane highway, you are driving slower than the posted speed limit. Which lane should you use?
choices: The center lane
Any lane, as long as you use your flashers
The far right lane, except when passing, turning left or avoiding an obstruction
The far left lane
explanation: When moving slower than the posted limit on a multi-lane highway, drive in the extreme right lane unless passing, turning left or avoiding an obstruction.

prompt: You are stopped at a steady red light and there is no NO TURN ON RED sign. What may you do?
choices: Turn right without stopping if the way is clear
Turn left or right after stopping
Nothing until the light turns green
Turn right after a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians
explanation: Unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted, a right turn may be made after a complete stop. You must yield to other traffic and to pedestrians in or about to enter the crosswalk.

prompt: You arrive at an intersection where the traffic lights are dark because of a power outage, and no officer is directing traffic. What should you do?
choices: Drive through if the road you are on is the busier one
Slow down and yield only to vehicles on your right
Treat it like a flashing yellow light
Treat it as if there is a stop sign on every approach
explanation: When a traffic light is out or malfunctioning, proceed as though the intersection has a stop sign on all approaches, unless an officer or another traffic control device is directing traffic.

prompt: You have a green arrow to make a U-turn, and opposing traffic has a green arrow to turn right at the same time. Who should yield?
choices: The right-turning traffic must yield to you
Whoever arrived first goes first
No one has to yield when the arrows are green
You should yield to the right-turning traffic
explanation: When both movements have their own green arrows at the same time, U-turning traffic should yield to opposing right-turning traffic.

prompt: What do blue reflective pavement markers on some North Carolina roads indicate?
choices: The location of nearby fire hydrants or water supplies
A lane reserved for buses
A wrong-way warning
A rest area ahead
explanation: In some areas, blue reflective pavement markers show the location of nearby fire hydrants or water supplies for fire fighters. Red markers indicate wrong-way movement.

prompt: While driving at night, you see red reflective pavement markers facing you. What do they indicate?
choices: A no-passing zone begins
A school zone is ahead
You are traveling the wrong way
A fire hydrant is nearby
explanation: Red pavement markers indicate wrong-way movement. If you see them facing you, you are going the wrong direction.

prompt: A freeway entrance-ramp meter is dark (showing neither red nor green). What should you do?
choices: Use the shoulder to bypass the meter
Proceed without stopping and merge as normal
Stop and wait for the meter to turn green
Stop, then go one car at a time
explanation: When a ramp meter is dark, you may proceed without stopping and merge or yield as normal. Stop on red; go on green.

prompt: How far before a turn must you signal on a street where the speed limit is 35 mph?
choices: At least the last 200 feet
At least the last 300 feet
At least the last 100 feet
At least the last 50 feet
explanation: Signal during at least the last 100 feet before turning or stopping. On roads with speed limits of 45 mph or more, signal at least the last 200 feet.

prompt: You plan to turn off a highway with a 55 mph speed limit. How far ahead must you signal?
choices: At least the last 50 feet
At least the last 200 feet
At least the last 100 feet
At least the last 500 feet
explanation: If the speed limit is 45 mph or more, signal at least the last 200 feet before turning. The faster you go, the farther ahead you should signal.

prompt: What shape are North Carolina state route markers (N.C. highway numbers)?
choices: Circle
Rectangle
Diamond
Shield
explanation: North Carolina route markers are diamond-shaped. U.S. highway markers are shields, and N.C. secondary road signs are rectangular.

prompt: Where is the yellow, pennant-shaped no-passing warning sign placed?
choices: On the left side of the road, at the start of the no-passing zone
On the right side of the road, at the end of the no-passing zone
Above the center lane
Painted on the pavement
explanation: The pennant is located on the left side of the road and points to the beginning of the no-passing zone. It adds emphasis to the rectangular DO NOT PASS sign.

prompt: What information does the blue Emergency Notification System sign at a North Carolina railroad crossing give you?
choices: The crossing ID number, the railroad's name and an emergency phone number
The time of the next train
The speed limit for trains
Directions to the nearest train station
explanation: All NC highway-rail crossings must post a blue ENS sign showing the crossing ID number, the railroad company's name and an emergency number to report problems directly to the railroad.

prompt: An ambulance with lights and siren is approaching from the opposite direction on a two-lane road. What must you do?
choices: Stop in your lane immediately
Drive to the right-hand edge of the road and stop until it passes
Keep going, because it is in the other lane
Speed up to clear the area
explanation: All vehicles, regardless of direction, must yield to an approaching emergency vehicle by moving to the right edge and stopping. The only exception is opposite-direction traffic on a four-lane limited-access highway with a center median.

prompt: When are you NOT required to pull over and stop for an emergency vehicle using its lights and siren?
choices: When it is coming from the opposite direction on any road
When you are already driving at the speed limit
When you are in the left lane
When it is traveling in the opposite direction on a four-lane limited-access highway with a center median
explanation: The pull-over rule does not apply to vehicles going the opposite direction on a four-lane limited-access highway with a center median. In all other cases, pull right and stop.

prompt: You are on a four-lane highway (two lanes each way) and see a tow truck with flashing lights stopped on the shoulder. What does the Move Over law require?
choices: Keep your lane and speed
Turn on your flashers and pass on the shoulder
Move into the lane not nearest the tow truck, if safe, until you are past it
Stop behind the tow truck
explanation: The law covers emergency and public service vehicles parked within 12 feet of the road with lights on. With two or more lanes in your direction, move out of the nearest lane until safely clear.

prompt: On a two-lane road, you approach a police car stopped on the shoulder with its lights flashing. You cannot change lanes. What must you do?
choices: Stop completely until the officer waves you on
Cross the center line to give more space
Keep your speed and drive past carefully
Slow down and drive at a reduced, safe speed until you are completely past
explanation: With only one lane in your direction, you must slow down and drive at a reduced, safe speed until completely past the stopped emergency vehicle.

prompt: You are traveling on a two-lane road in the same direction as a funeral procession. May you pass it?
choices: Only if the procession is moving below 25 mph
No, passing is allowed only on highways with two or more lanes in your direction
Yes, if no oncoming traffic is in sight
Yes, if you use your horn first
explanation: Drivers going the same direction must not pass a funeral procession unless the highway is marked for two or more lanes moving in that direction. Never drive between vehicles in a procession.

prompt: You are passing a car on a two-lane road and sound your horn. What must the driver being passed do?
choices: Come to a stop
Move to the right and not speed up
Speed up to finish quickly
Move left to block you if it is unsafe
explanation: The horn signal puts the passed driver under a legal obligation to help you pass by moving right and never speeding up. Speeding up and causing a crash is a misdemeanor.

prompt: You cross a four-lane highway whose two directions are separated by a median wider than 30 feet. How does North Carolina treat the crossing?
choices: Each crossing of the roadway is a separate intersection
It is one single intersection
It is treated as a roundabout
It is not an intersection at all
explanation: On four-lane highways separated by a median of more than 30 feet, each crossing is a separate intersection, so you stop and yield at each one as required.

prompt: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren is passing through a roundabout ahead of you. What should you do?
choices: Do not enter the roundabout; if already inside, exit first and then pull over
Enter quickly and pull over inside the circle
Stop inside the roundabout immediately
Follow the emergency vehicle through
explanation: Never enter a roundabout while an emergency vehicle is passing through. If you are already in it, exit first, then pull over to let it pass.

prompt: In a multi-lane roundabout, which lane does the North Carolina handbook say to use to go straight, turn left, or make a U-turn?
choices: Either lane, changing as needed inside
The shoulder
The left lane
The right lane
explanation: Typically use the right lane to exit right, and stay in the left lane to go straight, turn left or make a U-turn. Do not change lanes inside the roundabout.

prompt: A bicyclist is riding ahead of you inside a roundabout. What should you do?
choices: Honk so they move to the shoulder
Pass on the right using the truck apron
Stay behind the bicyclist; do not pass inside the roundabout
Pass on the left once inside
explanation: Drivers should not pass a bicyclist while inside the roundabout. Bicyclists stay in the middle of their chosen lane.

prompt: When passing another vehicle in North Carolina, at least how far to the left of it does the law require you to pass?
choices: Three feet
Six feet
Two feet
One foot
explanation: The law requires the passing driver to pass at least two feet to the left of the vehicle being passed. The same 2-foot rule is given for passing a moped.

prompt: On a curve or hill, how far ahead must you be able to see before passing is considered safe?
choices: At least 1,000 feet
At least 500 feet
At least 200 feet
At least 300 feet
explanation: Passing is unsafe and usually illegal on any curve or hill where you cannot see at least 500 feet ahead.

prompt: On a three-lane highway (one lane each way plus a center lane), where may you pass?
choices: In the center lane in either direction at any time
Only in the center lane where it is marked for passing in your direction
In any lane that is open
On the right shoulder
explanation: On three-lane highways, pass only in the center lane and only where it is marked for passing in your direction. The exception is when the vehicle in the center lane is turning left.

prompt: You are being passed and you speed up, failing to give way. A crash with injury or damage results. What can you be charged with?
choices: A misdemeanor
Nothing, because the passing driver is at fault
An infraction with no points
Only a warning
explanation: If you increase speed and fail to give way to a passing vehicle, you will be charged with a misdemeanor if a crash results in injury or property damage.

prompt: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in North Carolina?
choices: No closer than 15 feet
No closer than 10 feet
No closer than 20 feet
No closer than 30 feet
explanation: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or the entrance to a fire station.

prompt: On a street with curbs, how close to the curb line of an intersecting street may you park?
choices: No closer than 20 feet
No closer than 50 feet
No closer than 25 feet
No closer than 15 feet
explanation: Do not park within 25 feet of the curb line of an intersecting street, or within 15 feet of the intersecting right-of-way lines if there is no curb.

prompt: At an intersection with no curbs, how far from the intersecting right-of-way lines must you park?
choices: At least 50 feet
At least 15 feet
At least 25 feet
At least 10 feet
explanation: Where there is no curb, do not park within 15 feet of the intersecting right-of-way lines. With curbs, the distance is 25 feet from the curb line.

prompt: When is it legal to park on the shoulder of a North Carolina highway?
choices: Only if approaching drivers from both directions can see the vehicle for at least 200 feet
Any time you turn on your flashers
Only at night
Only within 100 feet of an exit
explanation: Parking on the shoulder is against the law unless approaching drivers from both directions can see the parked vehicle for at least 200 feet.

prompt: Outside city limits, how close to a fire or fire truck may you park?
choices: No closer than 400 feet
No closer than one block
No closer than 100 feet
No closer than 200 feet
explanation: Do not park within one block of a fire or fire truck in city limits, or within 400 feet outside the city.

prompt: An ambulance and police car are stopped at a crash scene helping victims. How close may you park?
choices: No closer than 25 feet
No closer than 500 feet
No closer than 100 feet
No closer than 50 feet
explanation: Do not park within 100 feet of an emergency vehicle that has stopped to investigate a crash or give assistance.

prompt: You realize you have entered an interstate going the wrong direction. What does the North Carolina handbook tell you to do?
choices: Drive on the left shoulder against traffic
Pull onto the right shoulder and stop, then turn around when the way is clear
Back up to the ramp you came from
Keep driving to the next exit
explanation: If you enter an interstate the wrong way, pull over to the right shoulder and stop. When the way is clear, turn around and head the proper direction. Watch for DO NOT ENTER signs to avoid this.

prompt: Which vehicles are NOT allowed on North Carolina interstates?
choices: Recreational vehicles
Tractor-trailers
Farm equipment
Motorcycles
explanation: Farm equipment may legally travel on most North Carolina roads, but not interstates.

prompt: A school bus is stopped with its stop arm out on a two-lane road. Which traffic must stop?
choices: Only traffic in the lane next to the bus
Traffic in both directions
Only traffic behind the bus
Only oncoming traffic
explanation: On a two-lane roadway, all traffic from both directions must stop for a school bus loading or unloading passengers.

prompt: A school bus stops to load children on a four-lane road with no median. You are approaching from the opposite direction. What must you do?
choices: Slow to 15 mph and pass
Stop only if children are crossing
Stop, because all traffic in both directions must stop
Continue, because you are in the opposite lanes
explanation: On a four-lane roadway without a median separation, all traffic from both directions must stop for a stopped school bus.

prompt: A school bus stops on a five-lane road (two lanes each way plus a center turning lane). You are coming from the opposite direction. What must you do?
choices: Continue with caution; only traffic following the bus must stop
Stop, because all traffic must stop
Stop only if you are in the left lane
Move into the center turning lane and stop
explanation: On a road of four or more lanes with a center turning lane, only traffic following the bus must stop. Be careful, because a two-lane road with a center turning lane requires both directions to stop.

prompt: A school bus stops on a two-lane road that has a center turning lane. Who must stop?
choices: Only oncoming traffic
All traffic from both directions
Only traffic following the bus
Only traffic in the turning lane
explanation: On a two-lane roadway with a center turning lane, all traffic from both directions must stop. Only roads of four or more lanes with a center turning lane or a median let opposing traffic continue.

prompt: You are on a divided highway with four lanes and a median. A school bus stops on the other side of the median. What must you do?
choices: Stop only if its red lights are flashing
Pull onto the shoulder and stop
Continue with caution; only traffic following the bus must stop
Stop until the bus moves
explanation: On a divided highway of four lanes or more with a median separation, only traffic following the bus must stop.

prompt: You stopped behind a school bus that was unloading. When may you go?
choices: As soon as the children are on the sidewalk
When the bus driver waves you around
After waiting 30 seconds
When the stop arm is withdrawn, the red lights are off and the bus has started to move
explanation: Do not pass until the mechanical stop signal is withdrawn, the flashing red lights are turned off and the bus has started to move.

prompt: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist, according to the North Carolina handbook?
choices: Change lanes, passing only with abundant clearance and no oncoming traffic
Squeeze by within the same lane if the cyclist moves right
Honk and pass quickly
Pass on the right
explanation: Pass a bicyclist only when there is abundant clearance and no oncoming traffic in the opposing lane. Changing lanes is the safest way, and regular passing laws apply.

prompt: Which bicycle riders and passengers in North Carolina must wear an approved bicycle helmet?
choices: All riders of any age
Those under age 16
Those under age 12
Those under age 18
explanation: All bicycle riders and passengers under age 16 must wear an approved protective bicycle helmet.

prompt: Under North Carolina law, what is the maximum top speed of a moped?
choices: 30 mph
25 mph
35 mph
45 mph
explanation: A moped has two or three wheels, a motor of no more than 50 cc and no external shifting device, and its top speed cannot exceed 30 mph.

prompt: What is the minimum age to operate a moped on a North Carolina public road?
explanation: You must be at least 16 years old to operate a moped on a public roadway or public vehicular area. DWI laws also apply to moped operators.

prompt: A farm tractor ahead of you slows down and its operator signals with the left hand. What is the safest response?
choices: Pass on the right shoulder
Honk and pass quickly
Stay back; the tractor may be turning left
Pass on the left because the operator is waving you by
explanation: Many farm-equipment crashes happen when the machine turns left and a driver tries to pass, mistaking the left signal as an invitation. Be patient; pass only when the operator moves off the road.

prompt: When does North Carolina law require you to use your headlights?
choices: Only from one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
Only when visibility is under 1,000 feet
Only on unlit roads
From sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is 400 feet or less
explanation: Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise and when visibility is 400 feet or less. They are also required whenever wipers are on due to bad weather.

prompt: It starts raining lightly in the afternoon and you turn on your windshield wipers. What else does North Carolina law require?
choices: Turn on your hazard flashers
Turn on your high beams
Nothing, since it is daytime
Turn on your headlights
explanation: All North Carolina motorists must use headlights whenever they are using windshield wipers because of bad weather.

prompt: You are in a crash in which no one is hurt, but the damage to the vehicles appears to be about $1,200. What must you do?
choices: Nothing, because no one was injured
Immediately report it to the nearest law enforcement officer or agency
Only exchange information with the other driver
Report it to DMV within 30 days
explanation: Report any crash immediately to law enforcement if anyone is killed or injured, or if total property damage appears to be $1,000 or more. Failing to report can lead to prosecution and suspension.

prompt: After a minor crash on an interstate with no injuries, both cars can still be driven safely. What should the drivers do?
choices: Drive to the next exit and leave the scene
Move the vehicles out of the travel lane onto the shoulder
Leave the cars exactly where they stopped for police
Stand in the lane to warn traffic
explanation: If there are no injuries or deaths, each vehicle should be moved out of the travel lane onto the shoulder if it can be driven safely under its own power.

prompt: What protection does North Carolina law give to someone who stops and gives aid at a crash?
choices: Protection only if they are a medical professional
Protection from civil liability, except for intentional wrongdoing
Full protection even for intentional harm
No protection; they may be sued for any mistake
explanation: The law protects people who stop and render aid at a crash scene from civil liability, except for intentional wrongdoing or unruly conduct.

prompt: Under North Carolina law, how far from the nearest rail must you stop when a crossing signal warns of an approaching train?
choices: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet
Within 100 feet but not less than 20 feet
Within 30 feet but not less than 10 feet
Within 15 feet but not less than 5 feet
explanation: G.S. 20-142.1 requires you to stop within 50 feet, but not less than 15 feet, from the nearest rail, and not proceed until it is safe.

prompt: You are crossing the tracks when the warning lights start flashing and the gates begin to lower. What should you do?
choices: Stop and back up
Stop on the tracks and wait
Get out and run
Keep moving; drive through the gate if it comes down
explanation: If the lights start or gates come down while you are crossing, do not stop or back up: keep moving. The gates are flexible and cannot trap you.

prompt: A patrol car signals you to pull over, but there is no safe place to stop right away. What does the North Carolina handbook advise?
choices: Ignore the signal until you find a parking lot
Turn on your 4-way flashers, slow down by about 10 mph, and keep driving to the nearest safe area
Stop immediately in the travel lane
Speed up to reach an exit quickly
explanation: If there is no obvious safe place, turn on your emergency flashers and reduce speed by about 10 mph to show you are aware of the officer, then continue to the nearest safe area to stop.

prompt: Your car breaks down on the highway and you need help. What does the North Carolina handbook suggest to signal for assistance?
choices: Turn on the high beams
Tie a white cloth to the left door handle or radio aerial and raise the hood
Stand behind the car and wave at traffic
Leave the driver's door open
explanation: Move completely onto the shoulder, have everyone exit on the passenger side and stand away from the vehicle, and tie a white cloth to the left door handle or radio aerial and raise the hood.

prompt: Who must wear a motorcycle safety helmet in North Carolina?
choices: Only riders without health insurance
Only passengers
All operators and passengers on motorcycles and mopeds
Only riders under 21
explanation: North Carolina has a universal helmet law: all operators and passengers on motorcycles and mopeds must wear a helmet that meets FMVSS 218.

prompt: A rider buys a 'novelty' helmet and sticks a separately purchased DOT sticker on the back. Is it legal in North Carolina?
choices: Yes, any helmet with a DOT sticker is legal
Yes, if it has a chin strap
Only for passengers
No, a DOT sticker added by the rider does not make the helmet compliant
explanation: A legal helmet has the DOT symbol permanently installed by the manufacturer. A separately supplied or purchased sticker placed by the rider does not make a novelty helmet compliant.

prompt: What kind of inner liner does a legal (FMVSS 218) motorcycle helmet have?
choices: A gel liner about 1/4 inch thick
A firm polystyrene foam liner about one inch thick
No liner, to stay lightweight
A thin, soft foam pad
explanation: A legal helmet has a firm inner liner of polystyrene foam about one inch thick. Non-compliant helmets usually have no liner or only thin soft padding.

prompt: How long is a North Carolina motorcycle learner permit valid?
choices: 18 months, renewable any number of times
24 months
12 months, renewable for one additional six-month period
6 months, with no renewal
explanation: The motorcycle learner permit is valid for 12 months and may be renewed once for an additional six months.

prompt: What restriction applies to a rider with a North Carolina motorcycle learner permit?
choices: Riding only on weekends
No passengers may be carried
No riding on roads over 35 mph
Riding only with a parent
explanation: The motorcycle learner permit authorizes the holder to operate a motorcycle without passengers.

prompt: A 16-year-old wants a motorcycle learner permit. What type of driver license must they already hold?
choices: A Level 2 limited provisional license
No license is needed
A full provisional license (Level 3), with a parent or guardian's signature
A Level 1 limited learner permit
explanation: Applicants 16 to 17 must hold a full provisional license and have a parent or guardian sign. Applicants 18 or older must hold a license issued by DMV.

prompt: Besides holding a full provisional license, what course must a motorcycle permit applicant under 18 complete?
choices: No course is required
The MSF Basic Rider Course or the NC Motorcycle Safety Education Program Basic Rider Course
A 30-hour classroom driver education course only
An online helmet safety video
explanation: Applicants under 18 must complete the Motorcycle Safety Foundation Basic Rider Course or the NC Motorcycle Safety Education Program Basic Rider Course.

prompt: What do you need to legally ride a motorcycle on North Carolina public roads?
choices: Only a regular Class C license
Only motorcycle insurance
A moped registration
A driver license with a motorcycle endorsement, or a motorcycle learner permit
explanation: You need a motorcycle endorsement on your driver license (provisional, regular or commercial) or a motorcycle learner permit before riding a motorcycle on public roads.

prompt: Which tests are required for a North Carolina motorcycle learner permit?
choices: Only a riding skills test
Only the regular car knowledge test
A vision test only
Vision, traffic signs and the motorcycle knowledge test
explanation: Required testing for the motorcycle learner permit includes vision, traffic signs and the motorcycle knowledge test.

prompt: The posted limit is 55 mph, but heavy fog has cut your visibility. How fast may you drive?
choices: No faster than is reasonable and safe for the fog, even if that is well below 55 mph
55 mph, because that is the posted limit
Up to 5 mph below the posted limit
At least 45 mph, so you do not block traffic
explanation: Never drive faster than the posted limit or at a speed that is unreasonable or unwise for existing conditions. You must often drive slower than the posted limit.

prompt: You are not towing anything and are driving a car on a North Carolina interstate with a 55 mph limit and posted minimum-speed signs. What is the minimum speed?
choices: 40 mph
45 mph
35 mph
50 mph
explanation: On interstate and primary highways, the minimum is 40 mph in a 55 mph zone and 45 mph in a zone of 60 mph or more. These minimums apply only where minimum-speed signs are posted.

prompt: You are stopped at a steady red light on a one-way street and want to turn left onto another one-way street. May you turn on the red light in North Carolina?
choices: No, North Carolina law allows only right turns on a steady red light
Yes, after a complete stop, just like a right turn on red
Yes, without stopping if no traffic is coming
Yes, but only between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.
explanation: After a complete stop at a steady red light, North Carolina law allows only a right turn (unless a sign prohibits it). The law does not allow a left turn on red, even from a one-way street onto another one-way street.

prompt: You are using high beams on a dark highway when a car approaches from the other direction. North Carolina law requires you to keep your lights from glaring at people within what distance?
choices: 500 feet
200 feet
300 feet
1,000 feet
explanation: When meeting another vehicle, you must dim or tilt your headlight beams so they do not project a glaring light at people within 500 feet in front of you.

prompt: Which of these is a place where the North Carolina handbook says you should NOT park?
choices: On a crosswalk, sidewalk or bridge
30 feet from a fire hydrant
50 feet from the curb line of an intersecting street
On the right side of a two-way street
explanation: Do not park on a crosswalk, sidewalk or bridge. Parking 30 feet from a hydrant or 50 feet from an intersection's curb line is beyond the 15-foot and 25-foot limits.

prompt: How close to the entrance of a fire station may you park in North Carolina?
choices: No closer than 15 feet
No closer than 25 feet
No closer than 50 feet
No closer than 10 feet
explanation: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or the entrance to a fire station. The 25-foot distance is for the curb line of an intersecting street.

prompt: Your light turns green, but a pedestrian who started crossing earlier is still in the street in front of you. What must you do?
choices: Let the pedestrian finish crossing safely before you go
Go, because your light is green
Honk and drive around the pedestrian
Go if the pedestrian is past the center of the street
explanation: If the signal changes while a pedestrian is still in the street, drivers must allow the pedestrian to complete the crossing safely.
